judge_panel.reason: The paper's claim is specifically about the region where linear dephasing is unobservable BUT turbulent dephasing could be observable — i.e., where Λ<1 (linear unobservable) yet Λ>1 (turbulent observable). From Eq.(16), ∆ψ_lin,golden ∝ f_Edd α^{-1} h_0^{-4}, so at the lower bounds f_Edd=0.3, α=0.1, h_0=0.03, the linear dephasing magnitude is ≈6.24×0.3×1×1=1.87 rad, which is less than 8/SNR_0=8/50=0.16 rad only for specific combinations. The paper explicitly notes in §4 and Fig.2 that for 'f_Edd ≳ 0.3, C ≳ 300, h_0 ≳ 0.03, and α ≳ 0.1, the linear dephasing is unobservable (i.e. Λ<1) while the turbulent dephasing could be observable,' which refers to the AND-region where all four conditions simultaneously make the linear torque sub-threshold while turbulence pushes it above threshold — a nuanced region visible in Fig.2 between the purple and cyan lines, not a simple evaluation at the lower-bound values.

The paper repeatedly states that "for fEdd ≳ 0.3, C ≳ 300, h0 ≳ 0.03, and α ≳ 0.1, the linear dephasing is unobservable" (e.g. §4/Abstract), but its own criterion says "a dephasing is observable if its more than 8/SNR" and Eq. (16) gives "Δψlin,golden = -6.24 (fEdd/1.0) (α/0.1)^(-1) (h0/0.03)^(-4) rad." At the stated lower bounds, |Δψlin| = 6.24×0.3 = 1.87 rad, which is far above 8/SNR0 = 0.16, so the AND-threshold statement is mischaracterized.
